g.text: The PaperQuiz ordering nearly reverses the aesthetic ordering: denser posters
answer more; the fill loop packs to a target density
Left: aesthetic overall vs PaperQuiz detail, nine systems; right: same model with and without the loop, same skill under Codex

g.text: P2P leads both Quiz splits: its portrait canvas is packed with near-verbatim prose, at some of the lowest aesthetic
scores. The Paper2Poster tool is close behind because its content is assembled from the benchmark's own Q&A
extraction. Author posters prune to headline results and place last on both Quiz splits.
The single-shot baselines are strong on content and intermediate on aesthetics; Reel sits deliberately between the
Aesthetic appeal is subjective and audience-dependent; the sub-criteria are scored by
VLM judges that stand in for, but do not equal, human preference — a higher score
means the raters prefer the poster, not that humans would. Comparison (i) also
changes prompting, call count, and budget, so it does not isolate the loop; Codex at
